title: TTFT variance: root-cause analysis and rollforward plan for customer escalations
creator: Samir Rao
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported large TTFT regressions (1.5--3x median) and tokens/sec drops across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments beginning 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC. The pattern: long-context prompts (>=4096 tokens) hitting quantized variants saw increased first-byte latency followed by sustained throughput degradation. Impacts were intermittent but repeatable for several tenants and correlated to a scheduler heuristic change rolled on 2026-03-12 that prioritized kernel packing for short-context requests.
impact_observed: Symptom: median TTFT increased from ~180ms to 420ms for affected workloads; tokens/sec fell by 30-60% on saturated nodes. Affected models: rdx-open-13B-quant, community-13B-int8 (variants with shared KV cache). Environments: Hosted (canary/region us-west-2), Dedicated reserved pools (gpu-pool-3), Private clusters where customers had heterogeneous mix of short and long sessions.
steps_taken: 2026-03-12 23:10 UTC: On-call alerted by customer SRE and internal SLO monitors; triage channel created (pager #17891).
2026-03-13 00:05 UTC: Reproduced locally with long-context synthetic workload; confirmed regression after scheduler heuristic change (kernel_pack_v2).
2026-03-13 02:30 UTC: Temporarily disabled kernel_pack_v2 in staging; observed TTFT return to baseline on staging when disabled.
2026-03-13 04:45 UTC: Scoped rollback candidate and prepared rollback runbook; coordination with infra and release engineers for Hosted and Dedicated pushback.
2026-03-14 08:00 UTC: Per-customer mitigations applied for top 3 escalations (pin to pre-change variant, increase reserved concurrency for short requests, enable per-tenant KV isolation).
2026-03-14 12:30 UTC: Deployed rollback (kernel_pack_v1) to a subset of affected regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1) as a rollforward/rollback hybrid; early telemetry shows TTFT improvements.
2026-03-15 02:00 UTC: Enabled additional telemetry for kernel selection, per-request context length, and KV eviction events; added dashboard panels for triage team.
root_cause_summary: The kernel scheduling heuristic kernel_pack_v2 inadvertently favored short-context packing which increased kernel switches and caused KV cache thrash for long-context requests. This was exacerbated when quantized models shared KV cache and when node saturation caused frequent eviction/repopulation of KV entries, increasing first-byte latency and reducing tokens/sec. The change passed microbenchmarks (short sequences) but regressions only surfaced under mixed real workload distributions.
rollback_and_rollforward_plan: Immediate: Finalize staged rollback of kernel_pack_v2 to kernel_pack_v1 in remaining affected regions by 2026-03-16 04:00 UTC (Coord: release-engineering).

Short-term: Introduce a conservative kernel selection flag (kernel_pack_mixed_safe) that: avoids aggressive packing when average context length in last 5s window > 1024 and limits multi-model packing on quantized variants.
Medium-term: Implement a KV-prefetch circuit-breaker that disables prefetch for tenants exhibiting >25% eviction rate in 30s window.
Long-term: Add workload-aware scheduler tests in CI that run mixed short/long synthetic traces and measure TTFT/tokens/sec to prevent regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Median TTFT for known customer traces returns to within 15% of baseline on Hosted and Dedicated after rollback/flags are applied.
Tokens/sec increases to within 10% of baseline for affected quantized models under the same synthetic mixed workload.
New telemetry panels show stable KV eviction rates and kernel selection ratios during 24h post-change.
Rollout plan documented and runbook validated with on-call and release engineers.
test_plan: Synthetic mixed workload: 60% short (<=64 tokens) / 40% long (>=4096 tokens) sessions across quantized and float variants.
Replay top-5 customer traces against staging and compare TTFT and tokens/sec distributions before/after flags.
Chaos test: artificially throttle NVME and force KV eviction to validate circuit-breaker behavior.
A/B rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 2-hour observation windows and auto-rollback if TTFT regresses >20%.
next_steps: Finalize and merge PR #6342: add kernel_pack_mixed_safe flag and default to disabled (owner: @aisha-p).
Ship emergency rollback to remaining regions (owner: release-eng) by 2026-03-16 04:00 UTC.
Implement KV-prefetch circuit-breaker prototype (owner: @samir-r) for quick toggle via console feature flag.
Schedule postmortem and customer communication draft for 2026-03-17.
